quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep hill ahead.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded water. Even shallow-looking water can hide hazards. Turn around and take another route.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Use your low beam headlights.
Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when following another vehicle.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When you cannot completely cross to the other side.
When the crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you cannot completely cross to the other side.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time on any track. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Press hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to see surrounding traffic. Release the accelerator and press the brake smoothly to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted where you cannot enter, such as one-way streets or the wrong direction of an expressway ramp.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They alert sleepy or careless drivers with vibration and noise when their vehicle leaves the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert sleepy or careless drivers with vibration and noise when their vehicle leaves the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn tired or distracted drivers they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down before exiting the highway?

options.text: About halfway through the exit lane.
As you approach the exit lane.
Right when you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your highway speed until you enter the exit lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When taking medicine, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Ask your doctor if it affects your driving ability.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if it affects your driving ability.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how any medicine will affect you while driving.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, lower your speed to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast makes your tires lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: Can drivers pass another vehicle by using the shoulder of a road?

options.text: Yes, when the shoulder is paved.
Yes, when the other vehicle is turning left.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never pass by using the shoulder. Other drivers do not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder without looking. Use the left lane to pass on multilane roads.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for other traffic, and continue carefully.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
Go to the next exit if you miss yours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Keep right if moving slower than other traffic. If you miss your exit, go to the next one. Never back up or make a U-turn on interstates.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you before proceeding.
Drive around the pedestrian carefully.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: The broken line side allows passing. The solid line side does not allow passing.

questions.question: When bright headlights come toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 pounds are allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming conditions. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic mean?

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line separates traffic going opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beams. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: When passing, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
After you pass the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough space.

questions.question: If someone passes you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down to let them safely return to the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let them safely return to the lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down and make it easy for the other driver to return safely. This helps avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see clearly to the side, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down at intersections. If you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Then inch forward until you can see traffic in both directions.
